In geometry, a right triangle or right-angled triangle is a triangle in which one angle is a right angle (that is, a 90-degree angle). The incircle or inscribed circle of a right triangle is the largest circle contained in the triangle; it touches all three sides. Let $a$ and $b$ denote the lengths of the legs of such a triangle and $c$ denote the length of its hypotenuse. The area $S$ of the incircle of the triangle is given by $S = \pi r^2$, where $r$ is the radius of the incircle.
